import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 82

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/82](https://www.erdosproblems.com/82)
-/

open SimpleGraph Filter

namespace Erdos82

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V]

/--
A predicate that holds if $S$ is a regular induced subgraph of $G$
-/
def IsRegularInduced {G : SimpleGraph V} (S : Subgraph G) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  S.IsInduced ∧ ∃ k, (S.coe).IsRegularOfDegree k

/--
$F(n)$ is the maximal integer such that every graph on $n$ vertices
contains a regular induced subgraph on at least $F(n)$ vertices.
-/
noncomputable def F (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k | ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), ∃ S : Subgraph G,
    IsRegularInduced S ∧ k ≤ S.verts.ncard}

/--
$F(n) / \log n \to \infty as n \to \infty$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_82 : Tendsto (fun n => F n / Real.log n) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
$F(n) \le O(n^{1/2} \ln ^ {3/4} n)$

Theorem 1.4 from [AKS07]

[AKS07] Alon, N. and Krivelevich, M. and Sudakov, B., Large nearly regular induced subgraphs. arXiv:0710.2106 (2007).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_82.variants.F_upper_bound :
    (fun n => (F n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => Real.sqrt n * (Real.log n) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos82

reformulations.difference: Lean takes the supremum of uniformly guaranteed lower bounds on regular induced subgraph sizes. AKS §1 defines f(n,1) as the minimum, over n-vertex graphs, of the maximum regular induced subgraph size.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each graph G, let M(G) be its maximum regular induced subgraph size. The defining condition for a candidate k is exactly ∀ G, k ≤ M(G). Its set of candidates contains 0 and is bounded above by n, so its natural-number supremum is a genuine maximum, equal to min_G M(G). An induced Subgraph S corresponds exactly to the vertex subset S.verts with graph G[S.verts]; restricting labels to Fin n is harmless under graph isomorphism. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved the subgraph/vertex-subset equivalence, the maximum characterization, and F_eq_min_max without sorry or reliance on either reviewed theorem.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked against the accessible cited paper. Regularity includes degree zero, as required by its independent-set remarks. Set.ncard is ordinary finite cardinality here, and the supremum cannot encounter an unbounded-set default. Scratch Lean proofs establish F(0)=0 and F(1)=1 and expand both asymptotic statements into their intended quantifiers. Real.log at 0 and 1 affects only finitely many inputs. A computable exhaustive graph/subset enumeration for n=0,…,5 returned extremal sizes 0,1,2,2,2,3. The solved tag on the upper bound agrees with AKS Theorem 1.4. The reviewed source file remains identical to the specified commit.
